key_insight: Augment flow-matching training with posterior-conditioned intermediate states to densify supervision and reduce variance, preventing flow collapse in high-dimensional image generation.
problem_solved: Flow matching provides only a single trajectory per training sample for high-dimensional images, yielding an extremely sparse, high-variance supervision signal that can cause flow collapse (memorization of source-target pairings and loss of sample diversity).
method: Generate additional intermediate states by sampling from a posterior conditioned on real data, producing multiple trajectories per training example.
Apply the flow-matching loss to these posterior-augmented trajectories to provide denser, lower-variance supervision of the time-dependent vector field.
Train the vector field with this augmented supervision so dynamics generalize across inputs and avoid collapsing to trivial/memorized mappings.
impact: Provides a practical way to stabilize and scale flow-matching for high-dimensional images, improving diversity and fidelity of generative samples and reducing failure modes that arise from under-constrained training.
visual_elements: Side-by-side trajectory diagrams: (a) sparse single-trajectory supervision leading to collapsed flows, (b) dense posterior-augmented trajectories showing well-distributed flows.
Pipeline schematic: prior → posterior sampling (conditioning on real data) → augmented trajectories → flow-matching loss → learned vector field.
Before/after sample grid: images generated by standard FM (showing mode collapse) vs Posterior Augmented FM (diverse, high-fidelity samples).
Chart showing training signal variance or loss landscape: high variance with sparse supervision vs reduced variance with posterior augmentation.
paper_authors: George Stoica, Sayak Paul, Matthew Wallingford, Vivek Ramanujan, Abhay Nori
